overview: On Raiatea, Taputapuatea joined sacred space, political relationships and ocean travel. Its archaeological landscape includes coastal ceremony and inland cultivation; its influence was a network, not automatically a bounded empire.

items.text: Marae in the Society Islands developed as paved courtyards with a raised platform at one end. Taputapuatea combined social, funerary and religious functions.
Outrigger-canoe construction and observation of natural phenomena enabled ocean journeys that sustained gatherings of chiefs and priests.
Upland valleys preserve terraces, habitation traces and food plants introduced for cultivation. These places supported life beyond the ceremonial centre.
The principal marae was dedicated to Oro. Its prominence was linked with Tamatoa chiefly authority, and stones were carried elsewhere to establish related marae.
The place remains significant through ancestral connections and transmitted knowledge. Community work to preserve traditions is part of its living history.
